key_insight: InfiAgent keeps an agent's working context strictly bounded for arbitrarily long tasks by externalizing persistent memory into a file-centric state abstraction, preventing unbounded prompt growth and accumulated reasoning errors.
problem_solved: Addresses failure of LLM agents on long-horizon tasks caused by unbounded context growth, error accumulation, and the fidelity/stability trade-offs introduced by compression or retrieval-based fixes.
method: File-centric persistent state: encode memories, plans, observations and artifacts as external files that the agent can read/write.
Bounded reasoning loop: include only immediate, relevant context in the prompt while relying on the file store for long-term state, keeping prompt size constant regardless of task duration.
Operational primitives: atomic read/write, diff/versioning, and controlled retrieval semantics to maintain information fidelity and reproducibility.
impact: Makes general-purpose autonomous agents scalable and reliable for infinite-horizon tasks by eliminating prompt bloat and reducing accumulated reasoning errors—improving performance, debuggability, and resource efficiency for practitioners.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: LLM agent <-> file-centric state store showing read/write loop and bounded prompt window.
Timeline comparison: growing-context baseline vs. constant-context InfiAgent across long task duration (error rate or latency vs. time).
State flow: schematic showing files for memory, plan, observations and atomic operations (read/write/diff/version).
Performance chart: task success or error accumulation across steps for InfiAgent vs. compression/retrieval baselines.
paper_title: InfiAgent: An Infinite-Horizon Framework for General-Purpose Autonomous Agents
paper_authors: Chenglin Yu, Yuchen Wang, Songmiao Wang, Hongxia Yang, Ming Li
